marks.gloss_en: לעולם אסיפא, ולאו אאבר אלא אבשר -- R' Shimon's 'pure' is on the last clause but on the FLESH, not the limb, so the dilemma about the limb does not reach him (= p_asefa_abasar)
the stam: rather, actually [R' Shimon is] on the last clause -- and not on the limb but on the flesh
דילמא טעמא דרבי שמעון התם הואיל ומעורה מעורה -- perhaps R' Shimon's reason in the first clause is that what is attached counts as attached (= p_zeira_hoil_umeure)
R' Zeira: perhaps R' Shimon's reason there is: since it is attached, it is attached
דתניא: the fig branch attached by its bark -- R' Yehuda deems it pure, and you [R' Asi] gave his reason as הואיל ומעורה מעורה
a fig branch that broke off and is attached by the bark -- R' Yehuda deems [it] pure
on the middle clause: R' Shimon's 'they were not made susceptible' because what cannot be fed to others is not food
ודילמא טעמא דרבי שמעון בההיא אי כדרבא אי כדרבי יוחנן -- perhaps R' Shimon's reason in that clause is either as Rava or as R' Yochanan [explained it]
מאי טעמא דרבי שמעון? אמר קרא מכל האכל אשר יאכל -- the hanging flesh of an animal that died cannot be fed to others, so it is not food
R' Asi: [R' Yochanan's reason was said] on the middle clause

ורבי שמעון מה נפשך: if death makes [the hanging limb] fallen, let it be impure as a limb from the living; and if death does not make it fallen, let it be impure as a limb from a corpse -- either way impure
רבי שמעון בעלמא קאי -- R' Shimon is not ruling on the mishna's case but answering the first tanna's implication that a corpse's limb in general imparts impurity: it does not (= p_beolma_kaei)
the stam: R' Shimon stands on the general case [of a corpse's limb], not on the mishna's
מן החי ולא מן המת? וקל וחומר: the living, who is pure -- a limb separating from him is impure; the dead, who is impure -- is it not all the more so?
דתניא: R' Eliezer: I heard that a limb FROM THE LIVING imparts impurity -- and to R' Yehoshua's 'and not from the dead?' he answers only 'so I heard'
R' Eliezer: I heard that a limb from the living imparts impurity
as 'the minor Pesach, not to eulogize' means all the more so the major one, so here: 'a limb from the living is impure' means all the more so from the dead
R' Yehoshua: Megillat Taanit writes 'the minor Pesach -- not to eulogize'; does that mean on the major one eulogy is allowed? rather, all the more so; here too, all the more so
דתנן: an olive-bulk of flesh separating from a limb from the living -- R' Eliezer: impure; R' Nechunya ben HaKana and R' Yehoshua: pure
דתנן: a barley-grain of bone separating from a limb from the living -- R' Nechunya: impure; R' Eliezer and R' Yehoshua: pure
an olive-bulk of flesh separating from a limb from the living -- R' Eliezer deems [it] impure
the limb and the flesh hanging from a person are pure
the stam: what is between a limb from the living and a limb from a corpse? an olive-bulk of flesh and a barley-grain of bone separating from a limb from the living is between them
the stam: now that you have come to this -- between the first tanna and R' Shimon too, the olive-bulk of flesh and the barley-grain of bone is the difference
